text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-The Norwegian Teachers' Association says it should become more difficult to graduate at education colleges. An Aftenposten survey showed that students at education colleges study less than 30 hours per week on the average.

-Carl I. Hagen, head of Norway's right-wing Progress Party, says he belives declining support for the ruling Labour Party is a reaction to its reluctance to increase spending on the elderly and hospitals. Norway can afford to grant higher pensions and improve the health sector, Hagen says.

-Norwegian authorities are recommending that the passengers and crew on board the luxury liner Hanseatic be evacuated because it is uncertain how long it will take to pull the ship from a ground off the Arctic island of Spitzbergen. The shipowner, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, has not yet decided what to do.
-The rising dollar led to a record close at the Oslo Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
-Norway's Aker RGI has bought three fishing vessels from Emerald Resource Management. The ships have a capacity of 375 tonns and will continue to operate off Russia.
-Norwegian shipper Fred. Olsen signed a six-year contract for its rig Borgland Dolphin worth 2.2 billion crowns on Tuesday. The rig will operate for Norwegian state-owned oil company Statoil.
